deviations.what: T024's two live-production-boot scenarios (boot refuses and names every missing role; migrate still completes on a production database missing every role) are covered by an in-process check-registration test plus the check function's own unit tests, not a subprocess against a real production-shaped database.
deviations.why: check_portal_roles_present is the first production_critical check to query the database rather than read settings. A genuine version of these scenarios needs a reachable PostgreSQL server (SQLite triggers fairdm.E101, which _check_production_configuration does not let SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS suppress). This environment has no Postgres reachable: no docker daemon, no psql client, and localhost:5432 refuses the connection.

concerns: fairdm.E300 is already check_celery_broker's id (fairdm/conf/checks.py, pre-existing, unrelated, not production_critical). T025's acceptance criterion names fairdm.E300 explicitly for the new portal-roles check, and every design doc in this spec (plan.md, decisions.md, tasks.md) assigns it the same id with no apparent awareness of the collision. Implemented exactly as specified; two different checks now report under the same id. manage.py check --deploy output and any future SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS entry naming fairdm.E300 cannot tell them apart. Renumbering either check is outside T020-T025's scope - flagging for a maintainer decision.

T021 (pre_delete/pre_save guards on Group, 'every ORM writer' per research R6 and this story's brief) breaks 7 pre-existing US-1 tests that reset state via Group.objects.all().delete(): tests/test_portal_roles.py::TestReconcile (5) and tests/test_apps.py::TestPortalRolesReconciliation (2). Confirmed empirically (a throwaway probe reproduced the mechanism before either receiver was written) and by running both classes after T021 landed - all 7 fail with ValidationError naming a shipped role. See D23.

T025 (check_portal_roles_present, the first production_critical check to query the database) breaks 6 pre-existing tests in tests/test_conf/test_checks.py that call `call_command("check", deploy=True)` with no database fixture enabled: TestCheckCommandIntegration (2) and TestDeployCommand (4, parametrised). Confirmed by running both classes in isolation - all 6 fail with RuntimeError: Database access not allowed. See D24.

Neither of the 13 pre-existing tests above (D23 + D24) was modified, per this story's explicit prohibition against editing a test authored in a different story. Both regressions are direct, necessary consequences of implementing the acceptance criteria as specified, not defects in the new code - every acceptance criterion for T021 and T025 is independently proven by this story's own new tests, which are all green.

The full pytest run (poetry run pytest, 601s) is red for exactly these 13 tests and no others: 2778 passed, 8 skipped (unchanged from the verified baseline), 13 failed. The numbers reconcile exactly against context.verified_base's 2767 passed: 2767 - 13 (now-failing, previously-passing) + 24 (this story's new tests, all passing) = 2778.
poetry run pre-commit run --all-files is fully green (trim trailing whitespace, fix end of files, check yaml, poetry-check, ruff lint, ruff format, mypy, deptry all Passed).

blocked.reason: Every acceptance criterion is met - TestProtection (T020) is green, proving the receivers work exactly as specified. But connecting pre_delete on Group disables Django's collector fast-delete path for that model, so a bulk Group.objects.all().delete() now sends pre_delete per row and is refused the moment it reaches a shipped role - the same setup step tests/test_portal_roles.py::TestReconcile (5 tests) and tests/test_apps.py::TestPortalRolesReconciliation (2 tests) both use, neither authored in this story. This story's brief prohibits modifying a test authored elsewhere and instructs marking the task blocked rather than doing so (see D23 for the full reproduction and reasoning). The implementation is committed and correct; the seven foreign tests are left exactly as they were.

Every acceptance criterion is met - TestPortalRolesPresent (T024) is green. Two things remain unresolved and outside this task's authority: (1) fairdm.E300 collides with check_celery_broker's pre-existing id, per every design doc's own assignment (see concerns). (2) Being the first production_critical check to query the database, it breaks 6 pre-existing tests in tests/test_conf/test_checks.py (TestCheckCommandIntegration, TestDeployCommand) that call check --deploy with no database fixture enabled - reasonable until now, since nothing registered under deploy=True ever needed one. Per this story's prohibition against modifying a test authored elsewhere, neither the id collision nor the six tests are touched (see D24). The implementation is committed and correct against every criterion this task itself sets.
